facts.text: Repeated nominally identical perception trials differ because of dust density, target reflectivity, lighting, rain rate, sensor contamination and stochastic software effects.
facts.quote: Repeated nominally identical perception trials differ because of dust density, target reflectivity, lighting, rain rate, sensor contamination and stochastic software effects

facts.text: Agreement between simulated and physical perception trials must be judged on distributions rather than single traces because nominally identical trials vary.
facts.quote: so agreement must be judged on distributions, not single traces.

facts.text: Rail validation is an established analogue for judging simulation-versus-measurement agreement using distributions.
facts.quote: Rail validation is the established analogue

facts.text: In the described rail validation trial, at least 24 simulation-versus-measurement comparisons are made for each quantity, drawn from at least 12 track sections covering all four test zones.
facts.quote: for each quantity, at least 24 simulation-versus-measurement comparisons are made, drawn from at least 12 track sections covering all four test zones

facts.text: The described rail validation trial evaluates statistics such as means and standard deviations across track sections.
facts.quote: statistics such as means and standard deviations across sections are evaluated.

facts.text: The described rail validation trial compared three validation methods: EN 14363 values, engineering judgment and formal validation metrics.
facts.quote: Three validation methods were compared in that trial (EN 14363 values, engineering judgment and formal validation metrics)

facts.text: The proposed validation method in the described rail trial sets validation limits on the set of simulation-versus-measurement deviations.
facts.quote: the proposed method sets validation limits on the set of deviations.
